description: Rename the Issue aggregate's two terminal domain events to faithful names (IssueClosed→IssueCancelled, IssueWorkCompleted→IssueCompleted) with canonical reverse-DNS ids, sweep every server and web consumer to the canonical ids, and backfill historical persisted IssueEvents rows so pre- and post-rename data share one vocabulary. Zero external behavior change.

tasks.title: Rename server terminal event vocabulary and sweep all server consumers
tasks.description: Rename the two Issue terminal union variants (IssueClosed→IssueCancelled, IssueWorkCompleted→IssueCompleted) in the IssueEvent union, update Issue.Close()/Complete() to record them, route IssueEventSerializer.BusType/Unwrap through EventCatalog.ReverseDns constants, drop the dead work-completed catalog entry, and sweep every server consumer keyed on terminal type ids (epic auto-done + epic closed-reconcile handlers, inbox projection, stage attribution, metrics querier, stage-population snapshot, reconciliation docs) to the canonical ids. The C# 14 union makes the type-name sweep compile-checked; the spec tests enforce the string-literal sweeps. Includes sweeping all affected server specs so legacy types/ids no longer appear anywhere in server code and new terminal events flow correctly end-to-end on fresh data.
acceptanceCriteria: Issue.Close() records exactly one IssueCancelled (carrying the reason) and sets status to Cancelled; Issue.Complete() records exactly one IssueCompleted (carrying the workflow run id) and sets status to Done
The IssueEvent union exposes IssueCancelled and IssueCompleted and no longer exposes IssueClosed or IssueWorkCompleted
IssueEventSerializer.BusType emits com.mohist.issue.cancelled / com.mohist.issue.completed sourced from EventCatalog.ReverseDns constants (no divergent inline literals); Unwrap has the renamed arms

EventCatalog no longer declares com.mohist.issue.work-completed; both com.mohist.issue.cancelled and com.mohist.issue.completed have real producers; com.mohist.issue.closed was never catalogued and is not added
The strings 'com.mohist.issue.closed' and 'com.mohist.issue.work-completed' and the type names IssueClosed/IssueWorkCompleted no longer appear anywhere in server src or tests
Epic reconciliation fires for both terminal events: completion drives auto-done readiness/next-issue advance, and cancellation releases the serial in-progress slot so the epic does not deadlock
Inbox projection subscribes to com.mohist.issue.completed and produces a completion-kind inbox item (deduplicated on replay); cancellation remains excluded from the inbox
Stage attribution projects done on com.mohist.issue.completed and cancelled on com.mohist.issue.cancelled; stage-population snapshot excludes cancelled issues and counts completed issues as done
Metrics querier terminal bucketing classifies completed vs failed/cancelled under the canonical ids (CompletedType/CancelledType consts replaced, ~6 references + doc updated)
dotnet build Mohist.sln succeeds with warnings-as-errors

Server specs pass: EpicAutoDoneHandlerSpecs, EpicReconciliationServiceSpecs, InboxProjectionHandlerSpecs (+InboxProjectionHandlerRealtimeHintSpecs), StagePopulationSnapshotServiceSpecs, IssueStageAttributionSpecs, IssueQuerierSpecs, IssueMetricsApiSpecs, BackfillIssueCompletedAtMigrationSpecs
tasks.output: Renamed Issue domain events + serializer/catalog routing + swept server consumers + updated server specs; green dotnet build and green server specs (npm test).
tasks.notes: Per design D1+D2+D3 (server half). Field shapes are identical so payloads stay wire-compatible. This task also covers the server-side requirements of specs/terminal-event-consumption/spec.md (epic reconciliation, inbox projection, stage attribution, stage-population snapshot, metrics bucketing). Historical persisted rows are reconciled separately in T-002; this task's correctness is asserted on fresh/new data.

tasks.title: Add backfill migration rewriting historical IssueEvents.Type to canonical ids
tasks.description: Add a raw-SQL EF migration (timestamped strictly later than 20260629120000_BackfillIssueCompletedAt) that rewrites the persisted IssueEvents.Type column for historical terminal rows in place: com.mohist.issue.closed→com.mohist.issue.cancelled and com.mohist.issue.work-completed→com.mohist.issue.completed. Modeled on the BackfillIssueCompletedAt precedent (no BuildTargetModel, idempotent, gated null check) with a symmetric Down that reverts to the legacy ids. Add a migration spec covering the rewrite, idempotency, Down, and that snapshot/status/enum are untouched, so pre- and post-rename terminal data classify identically after backfill.
acceptanceCriteria: A new EF migration file exists with a timestamp greater than 20260629120000
Up rewrites IssueEvents rows of Type='com.mohist.issue.closed' to 'com.mohist.issue.cancelled' and Type='com.mohist.issue.work-completed' to 'com.mohist.issue.completed'
The migration is idempotent: a second Up run matches zero rows and changes nothing
Down rewrites the canonical ids back to the legacy ids (symmetric, reversible in the event layer)
The migration contains no BuildTargetModel call (pure data backfill) and does not alter issue snapshot state, issue status, or the IssueStatus enum
After backfill, timeline rendering and terminal bucketing classify pre-rename and post-rename terminal events identically (no terminal issue dropped or double-counted by persistence era)
A new migration spec passes under SQLite with raw SQL (no real DB engine, no wall-clock)
tasks.output: New raw-SQL EF migration .cs (Up rewrites terminal Type rows, idempotent; Down reverts) + migration spec; spec green.
tasks.notes: Per design D4+D6. The new ids and the 'behave identically across eras' guarantee are only meaningful once server consumers recognize the canonical ids (T-001), hence the dependency. The historical 20260629120000 migration is immutable history and must NOT be edited; on already-migrated DBs it is historical-only and on fresh DBs both migrations are no-ops on empty data.

tasks.title: Sweep web consumers to the canonical terminal event ids

Includes updating the web tests so the registry exposes only the renamed terminal ids and live terminal events continue to invalidate issue queries, route to their handler, and drive rebase/merge outcomes under the canonical ids.
acceptanceCriteria: shared/lib/canonical-event-types.ts defines IssueCancelled='com.mohist.issue.cancelled' and IssueCompleted='com.mohist.issue.completed' and no longer defines IssueClosed or IssueWorkCompleted (or the closed/work-completed ids)
